The Worker-only HTTP kernel. `http.js`: `HttpError` (with `HttpError.of(code, message?, headers?, details?)`), `json`, `apiError`, `redirect`, `requireMethod`, `requireSameOrigin`, `requireMutationOwner`, `requireReadOwnerIfPresent`, `readBounded`, `readJSON`, `tickerParam`, `requireTicker`, `keepAlive`, `errorText`, `internalKey(namespace, path)` (the `https://flows-<namespace>.internal/<path>` Cache API keys) and `edgeCache` (`handle`, `get`, `put`, each failure a miss). `errors.js`: `ERRORS`, one frozen `[status, default message]` per code. `log.js`: `logFailure(level, event, fields, error)`, the one way the Worker writes an unexpected failure. The shape is built by `shared/flows-log.js`, a leaf the shared modules can import: `failureEntry`, `failureLine` and `emitFailure(sink, level, event, fields, error)` write one JSON line `{ event, message, level, route, code, ...fields, error }`, with `message` an alias of `event` for one release, `level` `warn` or `error`, `route` the caller's route or path, `code` the caller's or the error's own string code, `error` the text of the caught value or null, and reserved keys that a field cannot rewrite. Logging never throws (an unserialisable field falls back to a minimal line, a sink that fails is ignored). The Worker's sites, the live layer's injected `log` sinks, the reading, the AI failover and the rail's one-a-minute log all go through it; success is never logged or sampled, so it adds no events. `tests/server-log.mjs` holds the shape, drives a real site of each module, and scans the closure for a hand-built failure line. `server/` holds no top-level mutable binding, no comments and is excluded from the static bundle. The suite runs every helper against a verbatim copy of the helper it replaced over tables of requests, bodies, origins and tickers, holds every literal `new HttpError(status, "code"` in `worker.js` and `shared/` to the table's status, and holds the failure-log key order. Literal `new HttpError(` sites stay where they are (the ingest scans pin some); a module moves to `HttpError.of` with its own move.

The door itself is `server/door.js` and `shared/flows-door.js`, below.

The ingest door v2 in warn mode (B3a and B3), behind `FLOWS_DOOR_V2` (`wrangler.toml` [vars], shipped `warn` since 2026-10-24; only the exact word `warn` turns it on, so `enforce` is `off` until B3b). With the switch off the ingest route is byte for byte what it was, and `?op=` and `X-Content-Hash` are ignored. With `warn`, a non-archive, non-live write is inspected, its row gets metadata, and nothing is refused. `shared/flows-door.js` is the pure leaf (it imports `flows-live.js` and `flows-freshness.js` only): `canonicalize` (keys sorted; the volatile stamps `generatedAt`, `readAt`, `screenerReadAt`, `refreshedAt`, `producer` and `fresh.readAt` dropped; non-finite numbers and nesting past 64 levels named), `sha256Hex`, `inspect(key, text, { now })` (per-product structural findings derived from the dry-run emit, every payload of which passes with none: `not_object`, `missing_key`, `schema_version`, `depth`, `panel_shape`, `ticker_grammar`, `ticker_mismatch`, `session_format`, `instant_format`, `session_future` against the next session the calendar expects, `n_mismatch`, `column_length`, `units_missing`, `rows_type`, `row_shape`; range violations in the universe are flags that cost quality and are never structural; a pending placeholder has no required keys), the ordering tuple `(epoch, session, quality, asof)` with `quality = 4 x round(63 x ok base panels / base panels) + tier`, so a complete L1 (253) beats an L2 that misses a base panel (235) and a complete L2 (255) beats a complete L1, `casVerdict` (`new`; `unchanged` by canonical hash; `advance` on an equal or higher tuple; `superseded`), `regressionOf` (a later session's card that keeps under three quarters of the stored base panels), `assess` (adds `size_collapse` under 40 per cent of the stored size for the products whose size follows the universe, `stale_producer` and `hash_mismatch`), `membershipFlag`, `planOf` and `doorMode`. `server/door.js` is `createDoor({ store, ensureFlowsTables, storeGone, log })`: `write` (one batch reading the key's stored tuple and, for a ticker key, the universe's name list, then one write; the response gains `door { mode, chash, product, session, quality, epoch, asof, cas, would, flags, ring }`), and `operation` for `?op=batch` (up to 100 keys or 2 MiB, each judged on its own; archive keys, `live:` keys, `meta` and duplicates refused per item; writes in D1 batches of 16 that are bisected to the poison key when the store refuses one deterministically, and not when the failure looks transient, at most forty failed batches), `?op=have` (up to 90 `(key, chash)` pairs in one statement; answers `have` and `need`) and `?op=plan` (the nightly's planned card set for a session, kept as the row `plan`; an older session never replaces a newer one). Every would-have-refused finding lands in `flows_quarantine`, a ring of 200 rows (id is the position, pruned by id range; bodies of at most 64 KiB kept for the newest twenty; a per-producer brake that keeps no body after twenty events of one check in the newest forty). The regression guard only logs its count (`door would hold regressions`); a ring that cannot be written is logged and never fails an ingest. `X-Producer-Id` names the producer and `X-Producer-Epoch` declares its epoch. The enforcing compare-and-set SQL exists in the store (`doorWrite` with `enforce`) and is proved equal to `casVerdict` over every pair of 36 tuples, but no route passes it. The synthetic and fixture refusal is another row's hook and is not here. `tests/flows-door-v2.mjs` reads the dry-run emit and runs the leaf, the store and the route over the warn paths, the batch, `have` and `plan`, the off paths, the upgrade of an old database, the manifest triggers and the round trip off, warn, off, warn with row-content assertions, and plants twenty-one wrong builds that its batteries must fail.

AS r`, bare or aliased, over the rows a statement names, and a json_each nested in a correlated subquery once for each element of the scan it sits under. The eight emit consumers (`flows-card-render`, `flows-events-contract`, `flows-overlay-contract`, `flows-payload-shape`, `flows-positioning-contract`, `flows-strip`, `flows-ticker-contract`, `flows-unusual-contract`) read it instead of running their own. The golden suite (the first half of `test:pipeline`) hashes every emitted payload against the manifest, builds a second emit to prove two runs at one clock are byte-identical, and names the payload and top-level keys that moved; `node flows-pipeline-golden.mjs --write` regenerates the manifest after an intended change and `--against <emit dir of the old tree>` prints the leaf paths.

The extreme-value leaf (F-21): no imports. The generalised Pareto fit by a profile likelihood in the shape (`betaHat` solves the scale for each shape, `fitGpd` minimises over it with Brent's method), the 90% and 95% profile-likelihood interval (`profileInterval`), survival and inverse survival, and the pooled shape of exceedances over each name's own threshold with the name-level scale set to its mean excess times (1 - xi) (`pooledShape`, `pooledInterval`, `exceedances`, `exceedanceGroups`). The suite holds the fit to scipy on committed reference samples (`gen-moves-fixtures.py` writes `fixtures-moves-gpd.json` with the generator's hash), the one-name profile interval to 88 to 92% coverage over 2,000 samples, the pooled shape to within 0.02 of the truth at 3,200 exceedances with spread scales (an inverse-variance weighted mean of per-name shapes lands outside that band), and publishes in `fixtures-moves-bands.json` what every later window rests on: the production-class true model's observed over predicted exceedances at 3 to 6 standard deviations for one seed and for ten, and the pooled interval's coverage on the dependent daily world (`w1dWorld`, with sector factors, common volatility shocks and per-name scales) at 400 seeds beside the independent-names figures. The pooled shape's variance under dependence by date: `pooledClustered` (the score of each exceedance with the scale moving with the shape, plus the correction for the estimated mean excess, summed by day and squared over the squared curvature), `pooledJackknife` (delete-a-block over six blocks of days with every threshold re-estimated, a t interval on blocks - 1 degrees of freedom, `tCritical95`) and `dateBootstrapShape` (blocks of days resampled with replacement, seeded), the first two held to an independent numpy implementation with numerical derivatives (`fixtures-moves-cluster.json`). On the dependent world the unclustered interval covers 88%, 84%, 72% and 32% at market weights 0, 0.2, 0.3 and 0.5, the score sandwich 86%, 84%, 79% and 59%, and the jackknife 92%, 93%, 91% and 74% (400 seeds): the 85 to 95% line is met up to 0.3 and not at 0.5, where the shape's sampling distribution is set by the few extreme market days of a 500-day sample. Tail diagnostics and laws: `hill` and `hillCurve` (xi over the root of k as its error), `meanExcess` and `meanExcessShape` (the weighted slope of the mean-excess line, xi over 1 - xi), `thresholdStability` (the pooled shape across a ladder of quantiles and the lowest from which every higher estimate lies within the spread two nested samples allow), `semiParametricLaw` (an empirical body and generalised Pareto tails fitted on each side, with `sf`, `cdf`, `isf` and `quantile`, the signed or the absolute law) and `covariateGpd` (a log scale linear in covariates with one shape, Newton in the coefficients inside Brent in the shape, standard errors from the step-scaled Hessian, `covariateGpdSf`), each held to numpy or scipy in `fixtures-moves-tail.json`. Reference scale and challengers: `referenceScale` (the root mean square of the sessions that are not scheduled events; counting an earnings session is the planted wrong build `sigma-ref-includes-earnings`, which the kill matrix now arms and kills), `dateJackknife` (a delete-a-block standard error for any statistic of the exceedance groups), and `hierarchicalShape` (a random-effects fit: each name's exact profile likelihood in the shape on a grid, a normal prior on the shapes with its centre and spread found by marginal likelihood, shrunken posterior means) with `CHALLENGERS`, the registry in which the pooled shape is the one baseline, the hierarchical fit a registered challenger and the per-name fit the reference; the suite scores all three, and the hierarchical fit has 17% less error than pooling when shapes spread by sector-like 0.15 and is no better when they are equal. The canonical large-move targets, a leaf with no imports: the frozen definition table (35 ids: `move.k{2,3,4}.h{1,5}` with `.up` and `.dn`, `move.im{1,1.5,2}.h1`, `move.x{5,10,20}.h{1,5}`, `move.earn.im`, `move.earn.ratio`, `move.ret.h{1,5,21}` at the fifteen-quantile union, `move.live.res` as a reading, `move.z63.h{1,5}` as a sensitivity), its `TARGETS_VERSION` and `targetsHash` (a definition changed without a version bump fails the test's pinned history), `sigmaRef` (1.4826 x MAD of the trailing 252 regular-session, split-adjusted, break-free, non-event log returns, at least 200 else the name is not forecast and counted with the reason, `clockVersion` `sess-v0` with the weekend variance 0; a later estimate is a new id for new issues only), `impactSession(report_date, report_time)` (defined once, here), `threshold` and `resolves` (every event row carries a scale and a finite k, `move.earn.im` on `sigmaQE` of the impact session; a missing scale is `{ok:false, reason:"no scale"}` and resolves to null; the vendor's `implied_move_perc` is refused as a source), `earnRatio` within one track, `rarityText` (a k-multiple is always printed with how often such days occur for that name, the empirical route floored at 1 in 250, the model route at the audited `pFloor` it is given, the scan p printed `p below 0.00002` and never as 1 in N) and `cardField` (about 30 bytes a card). 670 names take about 40 ms of thread CPU.

The IV-days lens on Market's Extremes (Risers and Fallers, `Raw change` and `In IV-days`, on for the owner's account and off for members, the worker passing `rtIsOwner` to `marketPage` as `data-lens`) and the IV-days column in Home's Leaders. `m = chg / (iv30p / sqrt(252))`, with `iv30p` the previous trading day's 30-day IV (the vendor's `iv30d_1d`, never a current IV, which rises with the move and would rank the largest shocks lowest) and the vendor's `implied_move_perc` never a unit; a name with `iv30p` null or not positive is on no list, never zero; a name with earnings inside 21 sessions is ranked apart; the median and the count beyond 3 are over the clean names; one line of copy (`A ranking, not a test: no error rate measured.`) and the caption `IV as of the previous close.`, none of the words unusual, alert, screen or rare. The leaf is the oracle and the pages carry the one division, since a page cannot import a module; the test holds both pages to its digits. Market ranks one population at a time and names it: the whole nightly universe once the nightly for the live rows' session has landed, the live roster alone while the live session is newer, the nightly when the live rows are older or unavailable. Home reads `/api/flows/universe?cols=t,sec,chg,iv30p,ed` (14.5 KB of JSON for 670 names, about 3.3 KB gzipped) for the event mark and the nightly fallback. The order is held while a mouse pointer is on the module. Chromium against `page.route` stubs, no server.

The `universe` payload's column store (`UNIVERSE_COLUMNS`, one integer column per key, decoded by `units`) and its 100 KiB budget, shed by column priority when over. The run's `shed` list is the measurement that counts. `projectionColumns` and `projectUniverse` serve `GET /api/flows/universe?cols=t,sec,chg,iv30p,ed` (one to twelve column names, normalised and sorted, a 400 `invalid_cols` otherwise): the asked columns of the one payload row, about 14.5 KB for 670 names and five columns, kept in the Cache API for 300 s so a repeat read costs 0 D1 rows, never written over the whole universe's last good copy.

The client freshness helper (`FlowsUI.freshFrom`, `heartbeat`); every key a heartbeat reads registers its server verdict with the pill, which is the worst case over its sources, so a page needs no line per region. A second window shares it only when asked: `popout(path)` (a path on this origin) adds a random `w=<16 hex>` group token to the hash, opens the path on the current selection and joins a `BroadcastChannel` named for the token; the other window opens on that hash and joins the same channel, each local change travels once as a delta, a message that is not a valid selection is ignored, and a received change is never sent back. The Flagged now pop-out, `/flows/now/` (`nowPage` in `shared/flows-pages.js`, a member page in the one page array with no gate; a signed-out reader gets the sign-in page): a title row with a Back to Market link (`.mk-pop`) and one module `#pwList`. It fits one screen with no page scroll and no inner scroll at 1440x820, 1024x768 and 390x844. It loads `assets/css/flows-popout.css` for the shared pop-out layout and `.mk-pop`, plus `assets/css/flows-now.css`, which the Market page does not load. `assets/js/flows-now.js` reads `/api/flows/flowalerts` every 60 s, and sooner when the rail's `fl` topic speaks. `FlowsUI.defer(group, {when, el, label})` loads a group of scripts after the page's `load` event and returns a promise that resolves when they have run. A group is declared in the page as one `<i hidden data-defer="<group>" data-src="${v(path)}">` element per file (a list in one `data-src` is refused: the version scan cannot see past its first URL) and runs in declared order, one file after another: the next is requested only when the one before it has run, and the first failure stops the group, so a file never runs ahead of one it follows and a retry resumes at the file that failed. `when: "idle"` (default) waits for `requestIdleCallback` with a 1.5 s timeout; `when: "visible"` waits for `el` to come within 200 px of the viewport, then idle. Under `navigator.connection.saveData` the slot (`el`) gets a status line and a button and nothing is fetched until it is pressed; a failed fetch removes its script element, requests nothing further from the group and puts an unavailable line with Retry above the slot's own content, and the promise stays pending until a retry works. A second call for a group returns the first promise. `flows-ui.js` has one script loader, `loadJs`, shared by `defer` and the `FlowsUI.link` stub; `flows-dock.js` has the only other. The Unusual page loads `flows-net.js` this way (`defer("net", {when: "visible", el: #uaNet, label})`): the host is `.fn-host.is-slot` in the served HTML, so its height is reserved at first paint by container-query bands in `flows-net.css` (the mounted network's height at each card width, measured; the header's two-row wrap under 540 px too). When the alerts arrive empty, withheld, pending or failed, `flows-unusual.js` swaps `is-slot` for `.is-quiet`, whose own bands are the height of the network's empty state (about 450 to 790 px against 1,000 to 1,360 for the full scene), so the card is not a one-line message in a 1,100 px box once the network has mounted and nothing below it moves when it does; inside the Unusual page's one-screen stage `.fd-stage` instead lets the quiet host fill its own card and reserves nothing, because an absolutely placed card has nothing below it to move; a feed with rows swaps back. Until the module mounts it holds a table of the eight largest names by flagged premium with their lean by the convention, written by `flows-unusual.js` from the alerts it already has. `flows-defer-render` holds that nothing below the card moves when the network arrives, that the reservation never falls short of the mounted height by more than 6 px nor leaves more than 50 px empty at eleven widths on a fresh load, in the full scene and in the empty one (an empty feed and a 500 at 1440 and 390 px move nothing below the card, with a layout shift under 0.1), that a two-file group whose first file fails once requests nothing of the second and runs both in order after Retry, that Data Saver and a 404 leave the table in place, and that the request starts after the load event. `tests/flows-weight.mjs` weighs a route as its eager scripts plus the files `DEFERRED` lists for it (declared groups), the dock's `flows-ask.js` and the `flows-link.js` body, against a stated per-route allowance; it scans every `flows-*.js` for a second loader and for a `.defer("group")` call the route's `DEFERRED` entry does not list, runs the declaration checker on eight negative fixtures (a space and a comma in `data-src`, a file missing from `DEFERRED`, a table entry with no element on the page, an unversioned `data-src`, an element that is not hidden, a file that is also a script src, a file other than the table's), and prints the headroom of each route against the 1 KiB floor with the pending `EAGER_KERNEL` entries subtracted on live routes: the routes under the floor are the `BELOW_FLOOR` list, each with the row that relieves it, and the list must equal the computed set in both directions. The ticker's ceiling carries a named `TICKER_RAISE` (OD-08, 1,613 B, the cost of `FlowsUI.defer` on a route that defers no group): it is held at that size, asserted to be deleted as soon as the ticker defers as many bytes of group files as it was raised by, and printed on every run; the kernel entries state their size and a landed entry is measured against it (`FlowsUI.defer` 1.6 KB, so the V and L share of the kernel is held at 3.8 KB under the named `KERNEL_LIMIT` decision, not the 3.1 KB of section 2.10). `flows-defer-render` is Chromium with `page.route` and no server.

The Home page's deferred chunk (F-08 part a). `flows-overview.js` keeps the first-paint modules and the data reads; the painters of What changed, Volatility, Reporting and Headlines (`paintChanged`, `paintVol`, `paintEvents`, `paintNews`, `renderSpine`) are in this file, declared as `<i hidden data-defer="home-below">`, asked for with `FlowsUI.defer("home-below", {when: "visible", el: #hmChg})` and handed the helpers they use through `FlowsUI.homeKit` (the first-paint file publishes it before the chunk runs; the chunk calls `homeKit.attach` with the five painters and `homeKit.attached` says it has). Until the chunk lands, Volatility, Reporting and Headlines show their own pending state and Reporting's numeral is a dash with that reason. The render test is Chromium and `page.route`, no server: no request before the load event, none at 390x844 before Glance opens, the hero and first-paint modules painted before the request, data before chunk and chunk before data, a 404 with Retry, Data Saver, 390 px, and the lower tiles' strip, compact and glance faces. The ticker's Surface & terrain view, the second tab of the chart panel (`FlowsUI.tickerSurface`: `mount` and the pure `model.surface` and `model.terrain`), declared as `<i hidden data-defer="surface" id="ftSurface">` when `FLOWS_SCENES` is `on` (or `owner` and the member is an owner) and loaded by `FlowsUI.defer` when the tab opens. It replaces the old scenes module and the dock's Volatility surface and Gamma terrain buttons. Rows are the union of the gamma grid's expiries and the engine's, joined by `FlowsUI.tickerGlance.model.expiries`, so the chip row, the strike rail on the price view and these scenes read one list; a chip carries the engine's fit word (FITTED SVI, SVI, REPAIRED or NO FIT). The Moves significance test. A leaf over `flows-stats.js` alone. For each name, `z = chg / sig` in the name's own typical days; below 2 typical days it is not tested but counted in the correction with p = 1; earnings within 21 sessions, no typical day and no published count are refused with a reason. Otherwise p is the add-one exceedance rate `(hits + 1) / 253` at the nearest level (`f2` from 2 to under 3 typical days, `f3` from 3), conservative for a move inside the level. Benjamini-Hochberg runs across every counted name at q = 0.10 and a name is beyond the usual when its adjusted p is at most q. The smallest p is 1 in 253, so few names pass except on a wide day. Eight worlds are built on them: `client` (the real `uw()` against scripted faults: attempts, results and failure kinds match an independent statement of the retry rules, no call outlives its bound, the meter's count, classes and exact failure codes equal what the vendor answered and every failure sample carries only its code, time, page and attempt, the rate floor stays inside its range), unchanged, every card validates), `cards-plan` (the same with the failures handed in), `store` (a night's keys with crashes, stale carries, absent and unsessioned keys, skewed sessions, cut and unreadable listings, stale globals: the verifier's states, counts, predicates, completeness and ordering equal a restatement from the world's own bookkeeping, conservation holds, no false green and no false alarm, and its frozen inputs are never written), `contracts` (planted corruptions refused by code and path, synthetic names refused outside a test, canonical form independent of key order and stamps), `meter` and `stages` (the codes, samples, the failure summary and its byte budget, and each stage's failure line), and `volflow` (`volflow.mjs`: the vol-flow stage on the virtual clock, the real `runFlowLeg` and `uw()` at the 150 ms pace and the real store's `hold`, `publish` and `flushHeld` against a store that answers in 2 s, with scripted multi-leg pages (short, full, a refused later page, a refused or failing first page) and refused card-x writes: every held vol section lands, a name whose write lands is written once and never vol-only first, a merged write refused once is written again and one refused for good falls back to the held payload, the multi-leg tally and the meter's codes equal the script, and the flow leg's time stays within 1.2 times its vendor calls at the pace plus 2 s and 6 s a failing chain, which an inline write on the lane breaks). `tests/flows-pipeline-chaos.mjs` runs all eight for 300 seeds (`volflow` on every tenth) or, with `FLOWS_TRUTH_DEEP=1`, 20,000, prints a table, and on a violation prints the seed, the first broken invariant and the last events, with the command that replays it. The Relations tab on the Market page (`FlowsUI.relations`: `mount`, `model`, `pearson`, `partial`, `fisher`), under the `FLOWS_SCENES` switch. It relates the names that carry the day's flagged option windows, the data the page already reads from `/api/flows/flowalerts` and nothing else: each window's premium (and its net bullish premium, calls on the ask side and puts on the bid side minus the reverse, by convention) is put into ten-minute bins from its own `spanStart`, the twelve names with the most flagged premium and at least four active bins are kept, a bin with no window is zero, and every pair gets Pearson r, the Fisher z 95% interval on the bin count, and r in each half of the window. A pair is drawn only when its interval excludes zero, the absolute r is at least 0.3 and both halves keep the sign (`stable`); there are three relations (`Active together`, `Lean together` and `Beyond the market`) shown one at a time. `Beyond the market` is the partial correlation of the Active series after each is regressed on the mean of the kept names' standardised Active series (per half too), with the Fisher interval on n - 4 (one conditioned variable); it removes the day's shared flow burst, not stock-price moves, and says so. The page says how many of the pairs would pass by chance (5% of those tested), that windows arrive in bursts so the interval is too narrow, and that it is not a forecast. Fewer than 40 windows, 20 bins or three names is `thin` with the counts and no drawing; a failed or unpublished feed says so with its reason. It is a ring by sector (each node its ticker and its sector, every one labelled) beside a list of the tested pairs with a Show all dialog; under 900 px the ring and the list are a switch. The rail family in the route table: `flowsRtRows({ serveRt })` is three rows, `/api/rt/ws`, `/api/rt/snap` and `/api/rt/status` (the paths are `RT_PATHS`, declared beside the handler in `shared/flows-rt-routes.js`), each with `methods: ["*"]` and `auth: "none"`. The rail answers its kill switch before it looks at the method or the session, so a mistyped, absent or off `FLOWS_RT_MODE` is a 404 `rt_off` even to an anonymous `OPTIONS`, and only then does it take the session (401), the method (405 naming GET), the audience (403) and the topic list (400); the router therefore gates neither, and the row hands the request to `serveRt` bound in `worker.js` with `json`, `HttpError`, `requireSameOrigin` and the session reader. The prefix branch stays in the chain for every other path under `/api/rt/`, through the same bound handler, so an unknown path is still the kill switch's 404 or a JSON `not_found`. The suite compares the rows with the branch they replaced over 6,000 requests (every path, query, method, environment with the rail on, off, unset, without its binding and for members, caller and upgrade-header set; status, headers, body, the error and the session reads) and scans the Worker for the single bound call.

The vendor extras (Frontier lane 2, design in `docs/vendor-coverage.md`): per-name data the nightly now stores for every name it reads, so the dossier, the reading and Ask hold it without a member's vendor call. `shared/flows-vendor-extras.js` is a leaf over `flows-cross.js`, `flows-freshness.js` and `flows-vendor-core.js`. `PARTS` names eleven parts in two card-x sections: `dx` holds the seven slow dossier sources (`info`, `profile`, `financials`, `breakdown`, `estimates`, `analysts`, `ownership`) reduced by the same reducers the Worker uses, and `vx` holds four operations the spec documents and no code read before (`dividends`, `splits`, `etf` for ETF exposure, `ivp` for interpolated implied volatility). Every part is `{at, rv, x}` (read time, reducer version, extract) or a stub `{at, rv, shed: 1}`; `partState` is fresh inside `refreshS`, stale inside `maxS`, expired beyond it, outdated on a version mismatch, and a part that fails keeps the good one inside its maximum age (`mergeParts`). `planSlow` orders the due parts by how close they are to their maximum age (a missing or outdated one first, ties by a hash of ticker and part) under a per-night cap of 2,000 calls (`SLOW_CAP`, `FLOWS_EXTRAS_CAP`; `FLOWS_EXTRAS=off` turns the leg off); a 40-night simulation on 700 and 856 names holds the cold start to five nights and no part to a read past its maximum age. The reducers name their failures (`unshaped`, `type:<field>`, `empty`), keep dates as dates, and withhold every amount, factor, weight and volatility whose unit the schema does not state (`UNIT_STATUS`). `exercisePressure` is the early-assignment window for a short call: an ex-date after today and on or before the expiry flags it, an ex-date of today does not, one on expiry day does, the last exercise day is the previous trading day from the calendar, and an empty list is never read as no dividend. `fitSection` sheds a section to its budget as stubs, `shedNextPart` does the same one part at a time against the 60 KiB card-x ceiling in `SHED_ORDER`, a fresh stub is not read again before its maximum age, and `shapeHealth` rates a part's failures (above 5 per cent warn, above 20 fail, under 50 attempts report only). `scripts/flows-legs/extras.mjs` is the nightly leg: it reads each owned name's prior card-x, reads the due parts through the pool and the deadline, cleans descriptions with the dossier sanitiser, files failures by status (429 limited, 401, 402, 403, 404 and 422 plan and stored so they are not asked for every night, anything else failed) and hands `runMarketLegs` the merged sections for the card-x store, whose shed order now puts `dx` and `vx` first. In the Worker, `nightlyView` offers a usable `dx` part to `planFetches` as a cache part that is a hit for its own refresh age and never replaces a newer cache row, and the events and peers packets print the dividend, split, ETF and implied-volatility-percentile facts with the amount, factor and weight held back. `tests/gen-extras-fixtures.py` writes `tests/fixtures-vendor-extras.json` from the committed spec (synthetic, invented tickers, marked as not observed on the wire). `tests/flows-vendor-extras.mjs` holds all of it with 16 planted wrong builds of the leaf and 7 of the health gate, the leg, the Worker and the packet. `extrasChecks` in `scripts/flows-legs/health.mjs` carries `shapeHealth` into the nightly gate (a part above the failing line fails the night under the `extras-shape` code only when `extrasStanding` shows seven clean nights behind it and no failure the night before, otherwise it warns; one between the lines warns, one under 50 attempts is a note) and `meta.extras` records the night's calls, due, deferred and unread priors.
